constraint_review: Shaped and sized like a human fingertip, mountable on a robot finger: met at concept level. The design is 20.0 mm diameter by 22.0 mm long with 14.0 g mass and M2 plus dovetail mount, inside the 26 by 20 by 25 mm BioTac precedent and close to human size, with 2 mm overhang over an 18 mm finger width noted as acceptable. Detects contact forces as small as about 1 mN: met on analysis. The 1 mN Hertz spot of 0.470 mm diameter at 5.78 kPa gives 3.57 fF change on 0.269 pF base for 14.6 LSB above 244 aF LSB noise.
feedback:
Overall judgment: the working principle holds as a mechanical and electrical chain and the deciding numbers check, my main worry is 1 mm localization from a 0.47 mm spot on 2.00 mm pitch rather than 1 mN detection itself, I would let this go to detail design, and it compares credibly with the closest prior art. SpikeATac proves the same split static capacitive plus dynamic PVDF on-finger idea works at US$365 and 4 kHz, while this concept adds a ridged micro-siped Shore A 10 dome on faceted flats with gel and a deterministic fail-safe heartbeat plus slip interrupt instead of a learning policy, at smaller 20 by 22 mm size versus 45 by 32 by 25 mm.

What I checked and why it matters: I re-derived every deciding number from its physical relation and the board code. For the soft spot I used Hertz sphere contact a equals cube root of 3 F R over 4 E-star with E-star equals E over 1 minus nu squared, and mean pressure p equals F over pi a squared, which is the correct small-strain elastic regime for Shore A 10 silicone with nu near 0.5. The board simulation (E14) uses F equals 0.001 N, R equals 0.01 m and shear modulus 0.145 MPa for E equals 0.435 MPa, giving a equals 0.235 mm radius or 0.470 mm diameter and p equals 5.78 kPa. My recomputation gives a equals 0.234 mm and p equals 5.81 kPa, so the spot claim is sound and the diameter versus radius wording is consistent. Everyday scale is right: 1 mN is about 0.1 gram weight on a pinhead-size spot, giving kilopascal pressure well below grip pressures.

For transduction I used parallel-plate C equals epsilon0 epsilon-r A over d and small-signal delta-C over C near compressive strain with strain near p over E. The board base calculation (E26) with 1.50 mm square plates, 200 um gap and epsilon-r 2.7 gives 2.69e-13 F or 0.269 pF, which I confirm. The board delta-C (E55) as 0.269 pF times 5.78 over 435 times 1000 gives 3.57 fF, which I confirm as first-order correct at 1.3 percent strain, and counts (E62) as 3570 aF over 244 aF LSB gives 14.6 LSB, which I confirm arithmetically. This matters because 14 counts is usable margin if the 244 aF LSB at 9.00 ms update from the AD7147A Rev B datasheet (E41) holds in system noise, and that datasheet page was opened and read, so the claim is stronger than literature by search snippet alone. I flag as weaker the human size precedent (E60) and tactile acuity threshold (E23) and porous-sensor saturation background, which rest on search results whose pages were never opened, and the silicone friction mu 0.5 to 1.0 and primer bond strength, which rest on commercial pages or unopened searches rather than measured curves.

Functions all have means, so check zero passes. Conform has the ridged dome (SKIN), support has the nail-backed faceted core with mount (CORE), quasi-static transduction has the capacitive grid (CAP), dynamic transduction has the PVDF film (PVDF), location and slip decision have the converter plus microcontroller filter (BOARD), and message has the cable with interrupt (CABLE). The chief designer therefore needed no function with no means.

For size and mass limits in check one I added the parts along each direction. Diameter 20.0 mm must hold core plus flex tiles plus skin drape, length 22.0 mm must hold dome plus mount, and mass 14.0 g sums 4 plus 3 plus 1 plus 4 plus 2 g (E53). The stack concern is thickness: skin 1.5 to 2 mm plus gel 0.5 to 2.5 mm plus films could exceed the under 2.5 mm soft-stack limit that lets 1 mN pressure reach the films, but at concept level the stack can be chosen at the low end to meet the limit, so this is detail-design sizing, not a failure of principle. The width fit of 20 mm dome on an 18 mm finger implies 2 mm overhang, which is human-like and acceptable at concept with dorsal flex tail at 3.18 mm bend radius clear of rim slip.

For numeric limits in check one-b every stated number has a board value. Hold force uses Coulomb F equals m g over n mu with m equals 1 kg, n equals 2 fingers and mu equals 0.5 giving 9.81 N per finger (E85), which I confirm. Pressure at hold as force over pi times 5 mm squared gives 0.125 N per sq mm or 125 kPa (E93), which I confirm and which matches the Hertz radius at 9.81 N of about 5.03 mm, so the 5 mm assumption is self-consistent. Full-scale sweep (E64) as p-light times F over 0.001 to one-third power gives 213 kPa at 50 N, which I confirm arithmetically, but the linear delta-C model is outside its small-strain regime there at 48.9 percent strain, so the no-saturation claim to 213 kPa needs nonlinear dielectric treatment in detail design; it does not break 1 mN detection. Message rate (E52) as 64 bytes times 8 times 100 Hz gives 51.2 kbit per s, which I confirm, and power 0.0991 W (E51) and filter load 44 times 2200 equals 96800 MAC per s (E78) are confirmed arithmetically and are easily finger scale.

For duplicate values in check two I used the sourced ones. Radius 0.235 mm versus diameter 0.470 mm are the same spot, pressures 5.78 kPa light versus 125 kPa hold versus 213 kPa full-scale follow one Hertz scaling law, and the 53.6 to 96.8 ms micro to gross slip times with 43.2 ms gap (E38, E84) consistently leave room for the 30.0 ms detector window.

For flow continuity in check three the pressure chain skin to gel to PVDF to capacitive tiles to faceted core to finger and the signal chains capacitive tiles to flex to board and PVDF direct to board to cable to hand controller are each bridged by a named part and meet in the stated order skin-gel-PVDF-capacitive on flats, draped like cornea over compound eye. No part sits in two places and no gap is unbridged; the PVDF passing static pressure through 28 um film is physically plausible.

For worst case, light-touch detection is shown at 1 mN, grip is shown mid-range at 9.81 N inside the 213 kPa span, and slip warning 30.0 ms inside 43.2 ms gap with direct PVDF to microcontroller bypassing the 9.00 ms converter update correctly addresses the hardest timing case. Remaining risks of sipe tear, flex shake-plus-pull continuity and timed-loop closure are correctly test needs in feedback text, not acceptance conditions.

For meeting facts in check four there are no open blocking objections and all four members judged ready, with the chief designer selecting ridged solid skin over clear-pad optics and leaking fluid skin, split capacitive plus PVDF over capacitive alone, and heartbeat plus interrupt plus frame over frame alone, each for stated physical reasons. That settlement supports acceptance. I accept the concept as working physically and buildable from molded silicone, gel, PVDF film, polyimide flex, converter, microcontroller and printed core with ordinary molding, lamination and assembly.

Advice for detail design, not needed for acceptance: refine gel-broadened footprint versus 2.00 mm pitch to tighten 1 mm centroid claim when only one taxel is strongly excited; sum nominal versus maximum skin plus gel plus films against the 2.5 mm intent and pick thicknesses that preserve it; dimension the 20 mm dome plus clamp plus dorsal tail on the 18 mm finger to show rim clearance; and confirm effective AD7147A noise with averaging for 0.269 pF base and 3.57 fF signal. None of these changes the concept verdict that both stated limits are met.
